Bashkir

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    From Russian маши́на (mašína, “motor vehicle, machine”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [mäˈʂɯ̞.nä], nonstandard [mä.ʃi.ˈnä]
    • Hyphenation: ма‧ши‧на

    Noun

    [edit]

    машина • (maşina)

    1. motor vehicle, car, automobile
      Уйынсыҡ машина.
      Uyınsıq maşina.
      A toy car.
      Иҫерек килеш машина йөрөтөү.
      İśerek kileş maşina yörötöw.
      Driving a car while intoxicated.
      Ҡалаға барып етмәҫ борон машинабыҙ ватылды.
      Qalağa barıp yetməś boron maşinabıź vatıldı.
      Our car broke down before we reached the town.
      Биш-алты ғына йәшлек малай-ҡыҙҙар, машиналар араһында йөрөп, хәйер һорай.
      Biş-altı ğına yəşlek malay-qıźźar, maşinalar arahında yöröp, xəyer horay.
      Boys (and) girls of just five (or) six years old are asking for alms while they walk around cars.
    2. (colloquial) Any type of household machine, electric or mechanic device, such as washing machine, milk separator etc.

    ablative машинанан (maşinanan) машиналарҙан (maşinalarźan)

    Bulgarian машина

      Borrowed from French machine or Russian маши́на (mašína).

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): [mɐˈʃinɐ]
      • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
      • Rhymes: -inɐ
      • Syllabification(key): ма‧ши‧на

      Noun

      [edit]

      маши́на • (mašína) f (relational adjective маши́нен, diminutive маши́нка)

      1. machine (device or mechanism)
        пи́шеща маши́на ― píšešta mašína ― typewriter
        перална машина ― peralna mašina ― washing machine
        Дадох ръкописа на една чиновничка да го препише на машина — каза Елин Пелин.
        Dadoh rǎkopisa na edna činovnička da go prepiše na mašina — kaza Elin Pelin.
        "I gave the manuscript to a clerk to type it on a machine [typewriter]," said Elin Pelin.
      2. vehicle, machine (motor vehicle, airplane, etc.)
        Пред хотела спират леки коли и камиони. Повечето от тези машини са трофейни.
        Pred hotela spirat leki koli i kamioni. Povečeto ot tezi mašini sa trofejni.
        Cars and trucks are stopping in front of the hotel. Most of these machines [vehicles] are captured as trophies.
      3. (obsolete) steam locomotive
        Тренът беше готов и голямата машина, окичена със зеленина, пухтеше и изхвърляше бяла пара.
        Trenǎt beše gotov i goljamata mašina, okičena sǎs zelenina, puhteše i izhvǎrljaše bjala para.
        The train was ready and the big machine locomotive, decorated with greenery, was puffing and throwing out white steam.
      4. (historical) siege engine, military machine
        Докарайте обсадните машини!
        Dokarajte obsadnite mašini!
        Bring the siege machines!
      5. (obsolete) cooking stove
        Щом стане, ще запали машината в кухнята.
        Štom stane, šte zapali mašinata v kuhnjata.
        As soon as he gets up, he will light the machine [stove] in the kitchen.
      6. (figurative) machine, apparatus (organization, institution, or system)
        Досега светът не е познавал такава военна машина като германската.
        Dosega svetǎt ne e poznaval takava voenna mašina kato germanskata.
        Until now, the world has not known such a military machine as the German one.
      7. (figurative, derogatory) machine, automaton (person working mechanically without feeling or will)
        Неговата цел е да ни убеди, че ние сме нищо, боклук, че не сме хора, а само машини.
        Negovata cel e da ni ubedi, če nie sme ništo, bokluk, če ne sme hora, a samo mašini.
        His goal is to convince us that we are nothing, garbage, that we are not humans, but only machines.

      Etymology

      [edit]

        Borrowed from Russian маши́на (mašína, “motor vehicle, machine”), from Latin māchina (“a machine, engine, contrivance, device, stratagem, trick”), from Doric Greek μᾱχᾰνᾱ́ (mākhănā́).

        Noun

        [edit]

        машина • (maşina)

        1. machine
          жазатын машина ― jazatyn maşina ― typewriter
        2. car, vehicle

        Pannonian Rusyn

        [edit]

        Etymology

        [edit]

        Inherited from late Old Slovak mašina, or more likely borrowed from Serbo-Croatian машина / mašina, from German Maschine, from French machine, from Latin māchina, ultimately from Doric Greek μαχανά (makhaná).

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): [maˈʃina]
        • Rhymes: -ina
        • Hyphenation: ма‧ши‧на

        Noun

        [edit]

        машина (mašina) f (diminutive машинка, relational adjective машински)

        1. machine
        2. engine
          Near-synonym: мотор (motor)
          парна машина ― parna mašina ― steam engine
        3. thresher, threshing machine
          Synonym: трешка (treška)

        Declension

        nominative машина (mašina) машини (mašini)
        genitive машини (mašini) машинох (mašinox)
        dative машини (mašini) машином (mašinom)
        accusative машину (mašinu) машини (mašini)
        instrumental машину (mašinu) машинами (mašinami)
        locative машини (mašini) машинох (mašinox)
        vocative машино (mašino) машини (mašini)

        Russian

        [edit]
        Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
        машина
        Wikipedia ru

        Etymology

        [edit]

          Borrowed from German Maschine (“machine, engine”), from French machine, from Latin māchina, from Ancient Greek μᾱχᾰνᾱ́ (mākhănā́, “machine, tool”). Doublet of махи́на (maxína).

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): [mɐˈʂɨnə]
          • Audio:(file)

          Noun

          [edit]

          маши́на • (mašína) f inan (genitive маши́ны, nominative plural маши́ны, genitive plural маши́н, relational adjective маши́нный, diminutive маши́нка, pejorative машинёшка)

          1. (colloquial) car, motor vehicle
            попа́сть под маши́ну ― popástʹ pod mašínu ― to be hit by a car, to get hit by a car
            • 1964, Братья Стругацкие, “История первая. Суета вокруг дивана. Глава первая”, in Понедельник начинается в субботу, Детская литература; English translation from Leonid Renen, transl., Monday Begins on Saturday, New York: DAW Books, 1977:
              «Глупо, по-моему, делать из машины идола», — заявил я. «Глупо, — сказал бородатый. — Но не все так думают».
              «Glupo, po-mojemu, delatʹ iz mašiny idola», — zajavil ja. «Glupo, — skazal borodatyj. — No ne vse tak dumajut».
              “It’s dumb to make an idol out of a car,” I asserted.
              “So it is,” said the bearded one. “But not everyone thinks so.”
          2. machine
          3. (colloquial, dated) computer
            • 1964, Братья Стругацкие, “История первая. Суета вокруг дивана. Глава первая”, in Понедельник начинается в субботу, Детская литература; English translation from Leonid Renen, transl., Monday Begins on Saturday, New York: DAW Books, 1977:
              «А что у вас есть?» — «Что у нас есть?» — спросил горбоносый поворачиваясь. «Алдан-3», — сказал бородатый. «Богатая машина, — сказал я. — И хорошо работает?» — «Да как вам сказать…» — «Понятно», — сказал я.
              «A što u vas jestʹ?» — «Što u nas jestʹ?» — sprosil gorbonosyj povoračivajasʹ. «Aldan-3», — skazal borodatyj. «Bogataja mašina, — skazal ja. — I xorošo rabotajet?» — «Da kak vam skazatʹ…» — «Ponjatno», — skazal ja.
              “And what do you have to offer?”
              “What do we have?” asked Hawk-nose, turning around.
              “Aldan-three,” said The Beard.
              “A well-endowed machine,” I said. “Has it been running well?”
              “Well, how shall I say…”
              “I get it,” I said.
          4. (physics, colloquial) accelerator

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): [mäʃiˈnä]
          • Rhymes: -ä
          • Hyphenation: ма‧ши‧на

          Noun

          [edit]

          машина • (mašina)

          1. car, motor vehicle, automobile
          2. machine

          Ukrainian

          [edit]

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): [mɐˈʃɪnɐ]
          • Audio:(file)

          Noun

          [edit]

          маши́на • (mašýna) f inan (genitive маши́ни, nominative plural маши́ни, genitive plural маши́н)

          1. car, automobile, motor vehicle
            Synonyms: автомобі́ль (avtomobílʹ), (colloquial) авто́ (avtó), (colloquial) авті́вка (avtívka)
          2. machine
          3. mechanism
          4. (Canadian, dated) agricultural implement / farm equipment, especially a threshing machine, or tractor
